def-adversarial-threat-set-and-robust-ri:
## Definition

Let $(\mathcal X,\Sigma_X)$ and $(\mathcal Y,\Sigma_Y)$ be measurable spaces, let $\mathcal A$ be a measurable action space, and let $P$ be a probability measure on $(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y,\Sigma_X\otimes\Sigma_Y)$. A threat correspondence is a map $\Delta:\mathcal X\to\mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ with $\Delta(x)\ne\varnothing$ for every $x$. It is measurable when its graph $\{(x,x')\in\mathcal X^2:x'\in\Delta(x)\}$ belongs to $\Sigma_X\otimes\Sigma_X$. For a measurable predictor $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal A$ and a nonnegative measurable loss $\ell:\mathcal A\times\mathcal Y\to[0,+\infty]$, the pointwise robust loss is
$$L_{\Delta,f}(x,y)=\sup_{x'\in\Delta(x)}\ell(f(x'),y).$$
Its robust risk is the outer expectation
$$R^{\mathrm{rob}}_{P,\Delta}(f)=\mathbb E_P^*[L_{\Delta,f}(X,Y)] :=\inf\{\mathbb E_P[g(X,Y)]:g\ge L_{\Delta,f}\text{ and }g\text{ is nonnegative measurable}\}.$$
If $L_{\Delta,f}$ is measurable, this is its ordinary expectation. The supremum need not be attained. For a metric $\rho$ on $\mathcal X$ and a radius $\epsilon\ge0$, the closed-ball threat is $\Delta_\epsilon(x)=\{x'\in\mathcal X:\rho(x,x')\le\epsilon\}$. On $\mathbb R^d$, $\|u\|_\infty:=\max_{1\le j\le d}|u_j|$ and the $\ell_\infty$ threat is $\Delta_\epsilon(x)=\{x+\delta:\|\delta\|_\infty\le\epsilon\}$. For a binary classifier $f:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}$, the robust zero-one loss is $\mathbf1\{\exists x'\in\Delta_\epsilon(x):f(x')\ne y\}$.
def-two-class-spherical-gaussian-mixture:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an integer $d\ge1$, a vector $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, and $\sigma>0$, the two-class spherical Gaussian model is the Borel probability law $P_{\theta,\sigma}$ on $\mathbb R^d\times\{-1,+1\}$ defined by
$$P_{\theta,\sigma}(C)=\frac12\sum_{y\in\{-1,+1\}}N_d(y\theta,\sigma^2 I_d)(C_y),\qquad C_y:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(x,y)\in C\},$$
for every Borel set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\{-1,+1\}$. Thus $Y$ is uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$ and, conditional on $Y=y$, $X$ has law $N_d(y\theta,\sigma^2I_d)$. In the normalized model used below, $\|\theta\|_2=\sqrt d$. Independent training and test observations are drawn from the corresponding finite product law.
def-binary-feature-bernoulli-model:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $\theta\in\{-1,+1\}^d$, and let $0<\tau\le1/2$. The $(\theta,\tau)$ binary-feature Bernoulli model is the probability law $P_{\theta,\tau}$ on $\{-1,+1\}^d\times\{-1,+1\}$ defined by
$$P_{\theta,\tau}(\{(x,y)\})=\frac12\prod_{j=1}^d\left[\left(\frac12+\tau\right)\mathbf1_{\{x_j=y\theta_j\}}+\left(\frac12-\tau\right)\mathbf1_{\{x_j=-y\theta_j\}}\right].$$
Thus $Y$ is uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$ and, conditional on $Y=y$, the feature coordinates are independent, with $X_j=y\theta_j$ with probability $1/2+\tau$ and $X_j=-y\theta_j$ with probability $1/2-\tau$. The displayed masses sum to one because each coordinate factor sums to one over its two possible signs and the label weights sum to one. The uniform-prior experiment used below draws $\Theta$ uniformly from $\{-1,+1\}^d$ and then draws observations conditionally independently from $P_{\Theta,\tau}$.
alg-gaussian-mixture-robust-mean-classif:
## Definition

Input: an integer $n\ge1$, an integer $d\ge1$, and an ordered labeled sample $((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_n,y_n))$ with $x_i\in\mathbb R^d$ and $y_i\in\{-1,+1\}$. Compute
$$w=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n y_i x_i.$$
Output the vector $w$ and the binary linear classifier $f_w:\mathbb R^d\to\{-1,+1\}$ defined by $f_w(x)=+1$ when $\langle w,x\rangle\ge0$ and $f_w(x)=-1$ when $\langle w,x\rangle<0$. The zero-score tie is assigned to $+1$.
alg-coordinate-threshold-preprocessing:
## Definition

Input: an integer $d\ge1$ and a vector $x\in\mathbb R^d$. Output $T(x)\in\{-1,+1\}^d$ with
$$T(x)_i= \begin{cases} +1,&x_i\ge0,\\ -1,&x_i<0 \end{cases} \qquad (1\le i\le d).$$
lem-gaussian-vector-norm-concentration:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $\sigma>0$, and $G\sim N_d(0,\sigma^2I_d)$. For every $t\ge0$ and $s\ge0$,
$$\mathbb P(\|G\|_2\ge \sigma\sqrt d+t)\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),\qquad \mathbb P(\|G\|_\infty>s)\le 2d\exp\!\left(-\frac{s^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).$$
For every unit vector $u\in\mathbb R^d$ and $s\ge0$, each one-sided projection tail satisfies
$$\mathbb P(\langle u,G\rangle\ge s)\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{s^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),\qquad \mathbb P(\langle u,G\rangle\le-s)\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{s^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).$$
Consequently, for $d\ge2$,
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\|G\|_\infty\le 2\sigma\sqrt{2\log d}\right)\ge1-\frac1d.$$
lem-gaussian-sample-mean-signal-alignmen:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,n\ge1$ be integers, let $\sigma>0$, let $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|\theta\|_2=\sqrt d$, and draw independent observations $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ from the two-class spherical Gaussian model with parameters $\theta,\sigma$. Put $W=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_iX_i$, and define $\widehat W=W/\|W\|_2$ when $W\ne0$ and $\widehat W=e_1$ when $W=0$. Then
$$\mathbb P\!\left(\langle\widehat W,\theta\rangle\le\frac{2\sqrt n-1}{2\sqrt n+4\sigma}\sqrt d\right)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{d}{8(\sigma^2+1)}\right).$$
cor-one-sample-natural-classification-er:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|\theta\|_2=\sqrt d$, let $0<\beta<1$, and let $\sigma>0$ satisfy $\sigma\le d^{1/4}/(5\sqrt{\log(1/\beta)})$. Draw one training pair $(X_0,Y_0)$ from the two-class spherical Gaussian model with parameters $\theta,\sigma$. Set $W=Y_0X_0$ and define the unit vector $\widehat W=W/\|W\|_2$ for $W\ne0$ and $\widehat W=e_1$ for $W=0$. Define $h_u(x)=+1$ when $\langle u,x\rangle\ge0$ and $h_u(x)=-1$ otherwise, and define its natural error by $\operatorname{err}_{\theta,\sigma}(u)=\mathbb P_{(X,Y)\sim P_{\theta,\sigma}}(h_u(X)\ne Y)$. Then
$$\mathbb P_{(X_0,Y_0)\sim P_{\theta,\sigma}}\!\left(\operatorname{err}_{\theta,\sigma}(\widehat W)\le\beta\right)\ge1-2\exp\!\left(-\frac{d}{8(\sigma^2+1)}\right).$$
thm-robust-sample-upper-bound-gaussian-m:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d,n\ge1$ be integers, let $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|\theta\|_2=\sqrt d$, let $\sigma>0$, and draw independent training pairs $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ from the two-class spherical Gaussian model with parameters $\theta,\sigma$. Set $W=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_iX_i$ and let $f_W(x)=+1$ when $\langle W,x\rangle\ge0$ and $f_W(x)=-1$ otherwise. For $0<\beta<1$, if
$$0\le\epsilon\le\frac{2\sqrt n-1}{2\sqrt n+4\sigma}-\frac{\sigma\sqrt{2\log(1/\beta)}}{\sqrt d},$$
then with probability at least $1-2\exp(-d/(8(\sigma^2+1)))$ over the training sample, the $\ell_\infty$ robust risk of $f_W$ under $P_{\theta,\sigma}$ at radius $\epsilon$ is at most $\beta$.

In particular, if $\sigma\le d^{1/4}/32$, then each of the following two conditions is sufficient for $\ell_\infty$ robust risk at most $1/100$ with the same training-sample probability:

- $0\le\epsilon\le(1/4)d^{-1/4}$ and $n\ge1$;
- $(1/4)d^{-1/4}\le\epsilon\le1/4$ and $n\ge64\epsilon^2\sqrt d$.
lem-common-shift-robust-risk-lower-bound:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $\epsilon\ge0$, let $\mu\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\epsilon$, and let $Y$ be uniform on $\{-1,+1\}$ and independent of an arbitrary Borel random vector $Z\in\mathbb R^d$. Set $X=Y\mu+Z$, let $P$ be the joint law of $(X,Y)$, and let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\{-1,+1\}$ be any Borel classifier. For the closed $\ell_\infty$ threat $\Delta_\epsilon(x)=\{x+\delta:\|\delta\|_\infty\le\epsilon\}$ and robust zero-one risk defined by outer expectation, $R^{\mathrm{rob}}_{P,\Delta_\epsilon}(f)\ge1/2$.
lem-gaussian-normal-prior-posterior:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $\sigma>0$, and $n\ge1$. Let $\Theta\sim N_d(0,I_d)$, and, conditional on $\Theta$, let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be independent with law $N_d(\Theta,\sigma^2I_d)$. Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ be independent uniform signs, independent of $(\Theta,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$. Put $\bar Z=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i$. The conditional law of $\Theta$ given $(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n,Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)$ is
$$N_d\!\left(\frac{n}{\sigma^2+n}\bar Z,\frac{\sigma^2}{\sigma^2+n}I_d\right).$$
For $n=0$, with no observations, the conditional law is the prior $N_d(0,I_d)$.
thm-robust-sample-lower-bound-gaussian-m:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, let $n\ge0$ be an integer, let $\sigma>0$ and $\epsilon\ge0$, draw $\Theta\sim N_d(0,I_d)$, and, conditional on $\Theta$, draw $n$ independent training pairs $S=((X_i,Y_i))_{i=1}^n$ from the two-class spherical Gaussian model with parameters $\Theta,\sigma$. Let $\mathcal S_n=(\mathbb R^d\times\{-1,+1\})^n$, and let $F:\mathcal S_n\times\mathbb R^d\to\{-1,+1\}$ be a Borel learning rule; write $f_S(x)=F(S,x)$. Define $m(S)=(\sigma^2+n)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_iX_i$, with the empty sum equal to zero. Define the expected robust risk as the outer expectation over $(\Theta,S)$ of $R^{\mathrm{rob}}_{P_{\Theta,\sigma},\Delta_\epsilon}(f_S)$, using the same measurable-majorant convention as robust risk; when this random robust risk is measurable, this is its ordinary expectation. Then
$$\mathbb E^*_{\Theta,S}\!\left[R^{\mathrm{rob}}_{P_{\Theta,\sigma},\Delta_\epsilon}(f_S)\right]\ge\frac12\,\mathbb P_{V\sim N_d(0,I_d)}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{n}{\sigma^2+n}}\,\|V\|_\infty\le\epsilon\right).$$Consequently, if $d\ge2$ and $n\le\epsilon^2\sigma^2/(8\log d)$, then$$\mathbb E^*_{\Theta,S}\!\left[R^{\mathrm{rob}}_{P_{\Theta,\sigma},\Delta_\epsilon}(f_S)\right]\ge\frac12\left(1-\frac1d\right).$$
lem-finite-independent-sign-sum-tail:
## Statement

Let $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m$ be independent random variables with values in $\{-1,+1\}$, let $c_1,\ldots,c_m\in\mathbb R$, and put $V=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i^2$ and $S=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(\xi_i-\mathbb E\xi_i)$. For every $t>0$, if $V>0$ then
$$\mathbb P(S\ge t)\le e^{-t^2/(2V)},\qquad \mathbb P(S\le-t)\le e^{-t^2/(2V)},\qquad \mathbb P(|S|\ge t)\le2e^{-t^2/(2V)}.$$
If $V=0$, then $S=0$ almost surely and all three tail probabilities are zero. The empty sum $m=0$ is included with $V=S=0$.
lem-bernoulli-coordinate-posterior-odds-:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $0<\tau\le1/4$, and let $n\ge0$ be an integer with $n\le\tau^{-2}$. Draw $\Theta$ uniformly from $\{-1,+1\}^d$ and, conditionally on $\Theta$, draw $n$ independent observations $S=((X_i,Y_i))_{i=1}^n$ from the binary-feature Bernoulli model with parameters $\Theta,\tau$. For each coordinate $j$, define the posterior log odds $L_j(S):=\log\bigl(\mathbb P(\Theta_j=+1\mid S)/\mathbb P(\Theta_j=-1\mid S)\bigr)$; these probabilities are positive for every sample because $\tau<1/2$. Then for every $j$ and every sample $S$,
$$L_j(S)=\log\!\left(\frac{1+2\tau}{1-2\tau}\right)\sum_{i=1}^nY_iX_{ij}.$$Moreover, the coordinates of $\Theta$ are conditionally independent given $S$. For every $0<\delta<1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the joint prior-sample experiment,$$\max_{1\le j\le d}|L_j(S)|\le15\tau\sqrt{2n\log\!\left(\frac{2d}{\delta}\right)}.$$
thm-architecture-dependent-robustness-bi:
## Statement

For $w\in\mathbb R^d$, let $f_w(x)=+1$ when $\langle w,x\rangle\ge0$ and $f_w(x)=-1$ otherwise. In the following lower-bound branch, let $d\ge1$, $0<\tau\le1/4$, $0<\gamma<1/2$, and $0\le\epsilon<3\tau$. Draw $\Theta$ uniformly from $\{-1,+1\}^d$ and, conditional on $\Theta$, draw $n\ge0$ independent training observations $S$ from the binary-feature Bernoulli model with parameters $\Theta,\tau$. Let $g_n$ be any function from the finite sample space to $\mathbb R^d$, set $w=g_n(S)$, and use $f_w$. If
$$n\le\frac{\epsilon^2\gamma^2}{5000\tau^4\log(4d/\gamma)},$$
then the expected robust risk for the closed threat $\Delta_\epsilon(x)=\{x+\delta:\|\delta\|_\infty\le\epsilon\}$ of $f_w$, averaged over $\Theta,S$, and a fresh test pair from $P_{\Theta,\tau}$, is at least $1/2-\gamma$.

In the separate thresholded upper-bound branch, let $d\ge1$, $0<\tau\le1/2$, $0<\beta<1$, and let $\theta\in\{-1,+1\}^d$ satisfy $\tau\ge(\log(1/\beta)/(2d))^{1/4}$. Draw one training pair $(X_0,Y_0)$ from $P_{\theta,\tau}$, set $W=Y_0X_0$, and define $T:\mathbb R^d\to\{-1,+1\}^d$ by $T(x)_j=+1$ when $x_j\ge0$ and $T(x)_j=-1$ otherwise. Then for every $0\le\epsilon<1$, with training-sample probability at least $1-e^{-\tau^2d/2}$, the robust risk for the closed threat $\Delta_\epsilon(x)=\{x+\delta:\|\delta\|_\infty\le\epsilon\}$ of $f_W\circ T$ under $P_{\theta,\tau}$ is at most $\beta$.
